definition: A copy of data kept close to where it is used, so repeated reads are faster.
label: Caching basics

definition: The application reads the cache first and fills it from the origin on a miss.
label: Strategies

definition: A DNS record that points one name at another name. Not allowed at the top of a domain.
label: Record types

definition: Removing an entry from a full cache to make room, for example the least recently used one.
A read that found the data in the cache.
Hits divided by all reads. Higher means the cache does more of the work.
Removing or replacing a cached copy on purpose, before its TTL runs out.
A read that did not find the data in the cache, so it came from the origin.
Where the original data lives, behind the cache.
The DNS server that looks up names on behalf of a client, usually run by the internet provider.
label: How a lookup works

definition: A cached copy whose original has changed, or whose TTL has run out.
Time to live: how long a cached copy or DNS answer counts as fresh, in seconds.
label: TTL and propagation

definition: Writes go to the cache first and reach the origin later. Fast, but can lose data.
Every write goes to the cache and the origin together. Never stale, slower writes.
